BiblicalUsage: Beth-Rehob means house of the street, and it is named twice, at opposite ends of Israel's story. Judges 18:28 sets it in the valley by which Dan rebuilt Laish, far from Zidon, and 2 Samuel 10:6 shows the Ammonites hiring the Syrians of Beth-rehob to fight David. A road town, first a landmark for Dan, then a source of soldiers against David.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that a town on the road to Hamath could not stay neutral for long, and Beth-rehob did not try.
